The statement is false. It is a long-debunked myth (often exaggerated further to claim the Wall is the *only* human-made object visible from orbit or the Moon). 

The structure is typically only a few meters wide, follows terrain that is similar in color and texture, and lacks strong contrast. Astronauts (including those on the ISS in low Earth orbit and Apollo crews) have repeatedly reported that it is not discernible to the unaided eye under ordinary conditions; photographs that appear to show it almost always rely on magnification, image processing, or specific lighting/angles. Many other human features (cities, highways, airports, large mines, agricultural patterns, etc.) are far easier to spot. Reliable sources such as NASA summaries and astronaut debriefs confirm this. 

Final answer: no
